root_cause.text: fib6_nh_init() incorrectly uses fib6_is_reject() to classify loopback nexthop objects (with fc_dst=::) as reject routes, skipping fib_nh_common_init() and leaving nhc_pcpu_rth_output unallocated, which later causes a NULL dereference panic when an IPv4 route references that nexthop.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that "nexthop objects have no destination prefix (fc_dst=::), causing fib6_is_reject() to match any loopback nexthop" and that "the reject path skips fib_nh_common_init(), leaving nhc_pcpu_rth_output unallocated. If an IPv4 route later references this nexthop, __mkroute_output() dereferences NULL nhc_pcpu_rth_output and panics." The patch changes the condition from fib6_is_reject() to a direct check for RTF_REJECT flag.

bic_trace_step.reason: The newly introduced fib6_nh_init() function (lines 2914-3041) does not call fib_nh_common_init() or any equivalent initialization for the nexthop. When fib6_is_reject() evaluates true (for loopback routes with fc_dst=::), the function jumps to set_dev without initializing the common nexthop fields, leaving nhc_pcpu_rth_output unallocated. This matches the vulnerability root cause. No fix (such as calling fib_nh_common_init) is present in this commit.
